goals.title: The shape companion — a browser surface for shape sessions

why.text: Adapted from Superpowers' visual companion, widened from visual-design questions to exploring alternatives generally. A conversation surface: it shows things that do not exist yet to help the operator decide. Never a state surface — ledger browsing, runs, and reports stay native-app territory.

doneWhen: a shape session can push screens to the operator's browser and read back clicks with nothing but the skill vendored in this repo
the companion is a client of the quirks daemon (same port, same 0600 token) and can sit side-by-side with the native app

goals.title: The service — one Bun binary, CLI becomes an HTTP client

why.text: Bootstrap step 4. The authority boundary: only the service touches storage. Bind-or-attach, socket-not-pid liveness, loopback bind.

doneWhen: the CLI reaches the store only over HTTP, autostarts the daemon, and fails loudly — no direct-store path remains
a second client (the companion) consumes the same routes

goals.title: Runs — dispatch, the parent agent, honesty in code

why.text: Bootstrap step: runs. The only thing approved, once, over a plan you can read. The honesty properties are the product and get code + TDD; nothing on this path is interactive.

doneWhen: an overnight run executes tasks across harnesses, continues past failures, blocks dependents, and resumes with --resume
every verdict quote is verified against the retained transcript in Quirks' own code

goals.title: quirks report — what needs you, first

why.text: Problem B's answer: NEEDS YOU → PARTIAL → ACCEPTED, never chronological, one screen by default.

doneWhen: a real eight-task night reads on one screen without hiding a thing that mattered

goals.title: Harness and model tables

why.text: Surface state the system already computes: is each harness present, authorized, answering; which model each tier resolves to. Quota state belongs in a table that refreshes, not in doctrine prose.

doneWhen: quirks harness answers 'can tonight's run lean on codex' without reading a doc

goals.title: The judgment skills — discipline that used to be code

why.text: D17/D18: the CLI supplies facts, skills supply judgment. Deliverables, not documentation.

doneWhen: an overnight brief carries ground rules and the source-conflict + scope skills; design/breakdown flows exist for the two flags

goals.title: The native workbench — ledger, terminal, preview

why.text: Owner reprioritized 2026-07-27: the daily surface, built right after the service. Left: goals and tasks. Center: the agents' terminal. Right: a webview for previews and companion screens. Modeled on vercel-labs/native examples/workbench; the TS core stands — the SDK grew TS-tier pty + <terminal> since our spec.

doneWhen: the workbench is the daily driver: ledger pane live against the service, a real shell at center, companion screens in the right pane
run views render live in the same surface once runs exist
